data.description:
## Symptom

A Gerrit change that has satisfied both merge gates cannot be submitted by the identity the agent workflow is meant to use. Change 2986 sat at `Verified +1`, `LLM-Review +1`, `unresolved_comment_count: 0`, and `submittable: true`, and the revision-scoped submit returned:

```
HTTP 403
submit not permitted
```

## Root cause

The `rebar-review-bot` account is a Gerrit `SERVICE_USER`. Its group memberships are `Registered Users`, `Anonymous Users`, `Service Users`, and its own per-user group. It is **not** a member of `Contributors`, which is one of the groups the `rebar` project's access config references alongside `Administrators` and `feature-branch-drivers`.

Gerrit computes permitted actions per caller. Querying the change as the bot returns `actions: ['followup']` with no `submit` entry, while `submittable` is independently `true`. So this is an ACL outcome, not a transient fault and not a gate problem — the change really is ready, and this identity really has no Submit permission.

The bot's other capabilities are intact: it authenticates (`/a/accounts/self` returns 200), it reads, it votes `LLM-Review`, and it pushes to `refs/for/main` over HTTPS.

## Why this matters

`AGENTS.md` instructs agents to land their own work: "Land it yourself with revision-scoped Gerrit Submit once both votes are green." That instruction is currently not executable by the bot identity. The working arrangement is to submit with the Gerrit administrator credential from SSM instead, which is how change 2986 was landed.

That arrangement is wrong in three ways:

1. **It escalates routine landings to administrator.** Submitting is a mechanical action gated on two votes the submitter did not cast, so it does not need administrator rights.
2. **It couples the delivery loop to a human-scoped credential.** Any rotation or scoping change to the administrator credential silently halts all landing.
3. **The audit trail misattributes every merge.** The submitter recorded on each change is the administrator, not the identity that actually did the work, which defeats the session-hashtag ownership convention the project relies on under a shared bot account.

Note that this is a permission gap, not a gate weakness. The two merge gates are unaffected: the bot cannot vote `Verified`, and it cannot approve its own `LLM-Review`, so granting Submit does not let it self-approve anything.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The intended submitting identity can submit a change that has both required votes, without the administrator credential.
- [ ] The identity still cannot cast `Verified`, and still cannot approve a change it authored — granting Submit must not open a self-approval path.
- [ ] The permission is expressed in the project's checked-in access configuration rather than applied by hand, so it survives a rebuild and is reviewable.
- [ ] `AGENTS.md`'s "land it yourself" instruction is either executable as written, or amended to state the real division of responsibility.
- [ ] A merged change records the working identity as submitter, so ownership is visible in Gerrit's own metadata.

## Notes

The access config is not readable by the bot (`config_visible: false`), so the exact current Submit rules could not be inspected from this session and will need to be read with an administrator identity before deciding between adding the account to `Contributors`, granting Submit to `Service Users`, or creating a narrower group. Prefer whichever option grants the least beyond Submit on `refs/heads/main`.
data.title: Review bot cannot submit changes; every merge needs the admin credential
